plan_source: Wikimedia Commons File:General Plan of Fatehpur Sikri City India 1917.jpg (V. A. Smith, Akbar the Great Mogul, Oxford 1917, p.477; Internet Archive Book Images, 'No restrictions' per Commons)
frame: OSM local metres, origin 27.091111N 77.661111E (data/traces/fatehpur-sikri.trace.json), x east, y north
transform: o = a*(px - i*py) + b (complex, px/py in ORIGINAL 2896x1632 pixels); free similarity, least squares over 8 control points

control_points.name: Gwalior Gate (plan) / OSM monument node on wall, 'inferred' match
Tehra Gate (plan) / OSM monument node on wall, 'inferred' match

accuracy: control points read by eye from the 2000 px preview (+-15 px); residuals 3-25 m over a 1.5 km span; stated registration accuracy +-30 m near the palace core, worse towards the edges. The fitted rotation (37.8 deg) agrees with the plan's printed north arrow (about 38 deg); the fitted scale is 1.43 m/px against 1.33 m/px from the printed scale bar (+7%), so distances read off the plan are uncertain by that much. The last two control points are a guess that two unnamed OSM monument nodes on the wall are the plan's gates, so they weaken the independence of the fit.
outside_grid: The 1917 wall circuit, Delhi, Lal, Agra, Birbal, Chodanpol, Ajmir and Chor gates all fall outside the +-900 m terrain window (the window covers only the palace core and part of the south and west wall), so none is placed.
